svg.aria-label: A space-time field for one 400 metre street: distance along the street across, time upwards, and one cell for every row of meo_exposure_samples. The shadow's edge steps 6.8 metres right at every 3-minute timestep, so the two walks — opposite diagonals through the same field — cross it in different places: 504 seconds of sun one way against 492 the other, and 252 against 246 metres of continuous exposure. A per-edge sum reports 532 seconds for both.
svg.text: A walk is a diagonal cut through the table
One cell = one row of meo_exposure_samples (2 m × 3 min). Walking east and walking west read different cells.

The same field, read along each diagonal — what each walker experiences, in order
Each strip runs from its walker's entry. Dashed: where a frozen shadow would put the boundary — the real one has moved by the time the walker reaches it.
Both directions cross the same 201 samples, so the per-edge sunlit_sum — 133 of 201 at 16:00 — is identical for the two.
It is also the frozen answer, 532 s: the moving shadow costs the forward walker 28 s of that and the reverse walker 40 s. The 12 s
between them exists only in the ordered, per-sample series — which is why v2 keeps v1's 7,886,872,800 sample rows rather than
